study_type.claude: Mixed methods (multi-phase: diary study, follow-up interviews, daily surveys, logs-based signals, validation against self-report)
study_type.nlm: Mixed methods (diary study, interviews, daily end-of-day surveys, logs-based modeling via word2vec, quarterly surveys)
study_type.note: Claude describes the article genre as a magazine column / industrial practice report, but its method description is the same multi-phase mixed design. Sample sizes not reported, so the author may prefer Experience report.

research_method.claude: Multi-phase human-centered approach: (1) diary study, follow-up interviews and end-of-day daily surveys; (2) logs-based signals (word2vec over cross-tool log sequences; friction components vs thresholds); (3) validation against diaries and quarterly longitudinal survey; sample sizes not reported
research_method.nlm: Mixed methods: qualitative diary study, follow-up interviews, daily end-of-day surveys for a week, cross-tool logs modeling via word2vec, quarterly longitudinal surveys; thresholds via classification
research_method.value: Multi-phase human-centered metric development: (1) diary study with follow-up interviews and end-of-day surveys over one week to capture experienced flow and friction; (2) logs-based metrics: focus time from word2vec task similarity over cross-tool log sequences, and a composite friction metric (build/test latency, flaky tests, blocked submissions aggregated per developer-day, thresholds set as a classification problem); (3) validation against diary data and a quarterly longitudinal survey; sample sizes not reported

cat_satisfaction.note: Quarterly survey sentiment items (satisfaction with code complexity, project velocity, tools, development speed) used to validate friction thresholds.

cat_activity.note: Number of change lists; number of builds discussed critically; logged events/sessions used as controls.

cat_delivery.note: Thin: latency of tests tied to change-list submission and CI-blocked submission attempts, labelled Delivery by both.

cat_devex.note: Flow/focus and friction are measured and labelled DevEx by both, but the DevEx framework (Noda/Storey/Forsgren) is not cited; Google's own line of work.

cat_agile.note: NotebookLM labels blocked submissions 'Process / Delivery', but it is a CI friction component, not an agile/process metric.

cat_survey.note: Diary study, end-of-day surveys, interviews and a quarterly survey item on flow.

evidence.quote: by: 1) understanding developers’ subjective experiences, 2) identifying logs-based signals that most closely represent these experiences, and 3) validating our metrics against self-reported data.
We conducted a diary study with follow-up interviews to hear from developers directly and identify generalizable characteristics of flow that informed our logs-based metric.
To do this, we surveyed a sample of developers at the end of their workday each day for a week to better understand whether they experienced friction
we validated that our metric was capturing the behaviors of interest using diary data and quarterly survey
